# wazmrt conformance baseline — EXPECTED failures per .wast file.
# Generated by `zig build conformance -Dtestsuite=<dir> -Dwrite-baseline=true`.
# The step fails only when a file does WORSE than its line here, so this
# gates against regressions rather than against a zero that upstream has
# never reached. A file that improves is reported, not failed — re-generate
# to lock the improvement in. `error <path>` = the runner cannot parse it.
#
# ⚠️ A BASELINE IS ONLY HONEST IF EVERY LINE HAS A REASON. Otherwise it is a
# way to make a red number green. Every entry below falls into one of three
# groups. ✅ **ALL FOUR GROUPS ARE NOW EMPTY.** The corpus is at **ZERO FAILURES**
# across all 284 files, and the single remaining line is `annotations.wast` — a
# runner-LEX gap on the untargeted custom-annotations proposal, which is a runner
# error rather than a failure. The groups below are kept as the record of what was
# closed and why; each closure is more instructive than the entry it replaced:
#
#   1. UNTARGETED PROPOSALS — **NONE. This group is EMPTY.** custom-descriptors
#      is fully implemented as of 2026-08-17 (D1–D5), so there is no longer any
#      proposal wazmrt refuses — except `custom-annotations`, whose one line is
#      the last entry in this file (a runner-lex gap, not a failure).
#
#      Kept for the record, because the shape of the closure is the useful part:
#
#      custom-descriptors — ALL of it ships.
#        ✅ D1 (2026-08-17): the `(exact $t)` reference-type former, with
#          subtyping enforced.
#        ✅ D2 (2026-08-17): `(descriptor $d)` / `(describes $s)` in text and
#          binary (`0x4c`/`0x4d`, `describes` first), their validation rules, and
#          the descriptor links folded into all three type-identity keys
#          (`Module.canonicalizeTypes`, `interp.groupKey`, `typematch.eqMember`).
#          `descriptors.wast` 21 failures -> 0, `binary-descriptors.wast` 2 -> 0.
#        ✅ D3 (2026-08-17): `struct.new_desc` / `struct.new_default_desc` /
#          `ref.get_desc` (`0xFB 0x20`/`0x21`/`0x22`), the descriptor carried as a
#          VALUE on every heap object, and exactness propagation.
#          `struct_new_desc.wast` and `ref_get_desc.wast` both 0.
#        ✅ D5 (2026-08-17, with D3): every GC allocation produces an EXACT
#          reference. `array_new_exact.wast` 1 -> 0.
#        ✅ D4 (2026-08-17): `ref.cast_desc_eq` (`0xFB 0x23`/`0x24`) and
#          `br_on_cast_desc_eq`/`_fail` (`0x25`/`0x26`) — casts that compare the
#          value's descriptor by OBJECT IDENTITY. All three files 0 failed /
#          0 skipped. It was carried here as TWO failures and was worth **353
#          SKIPS**; the roadmap said to size it by those and it was right.
#          That is the R3/R5/P lesson for the sixth time.
#
#      ⚠️ **D4 also had to add a `custom_descriptors` FEATURE, and the reason is
#      new:** the proposal RETYPES an existing instruction. `br_on_cast` requires
#      a downcast (`rt2 <: rt1`) in the merged spec and only a shared top type
#      under custom-descriptors, so `br_on_cast 0 eqref anyref` is
#      `assert_invalid` in the CORE `br_on_cast.wast` and a VALID module in the
#      proposal's copy of the same file. No single answer satisfies both, so
#      `wast.featuresForPath` judges each by its era — the machinery F4 built for
#      `proposals/threads`, used here for the first time in the other direction:
#      this is the one entry that is opt-IN by directory, because the era that
#      LACKS the proposal is the merged spec, i.e. every other file.
#
#        ⚠️ **D2, D3 and D4 all moved the grand TOTAL down while closing
#        failures, and every time that was correct.** Modules that had been
#        assembling with a clause silently DROPPED were running assertions against
#        a module the file did not write; assembled correctly they are refused at
#        the next unimplemented instruction, i.e. a skip. And a module that FAILS
#        to build contributes one countable failure while one that BUILDS
#        contributes nothing, so every module that starts building removes an
#        assertion from the corpus total. D2: 63,344/53/515 -> 63,315/16/578.
#        D3: -> 63,391/4/497. D4: -> 63,731/2/144 (+340 passes, -353 skips,
#        -15 total). **Read all three columns and expect the total to move.**
#
#      custom-page-sizes — ✅ IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-17, group entry removed. All
#        four files are now 0 failed / 0 SKIPPED (61 assertions passing, up from
#        5 passed / 2 failed / 69 skipped).
#
#        ⚠️ **It was carried here as "2 assertions" and it was worth 69 skips** —
#        the failure column undercounted it by 35x, because a module the
#        assembler could not build sends every assertion targeting it into
#        `NoTarget`. That is the third time this list has re-learned to rank by
#        ASSERTIONS UNBLOCKED rather than failures closed (R3, R5, and now P).
#        **Read the skip column beside the failure count before sizing an item.**
#
#   2. ERA-PINNED SNAPSHOT (proposals/threads) — CLOSED 2026-08-17, 0 assertions.
#      ✅ This group is EMPTY and its two lines are gone from the list below.
#
#      It read: that directory predates multi-memory and multi-table, so it
#      asserts `(module (memory 0) (memory 0))` is INVALID; wazmrt implements
#      both, so accepting those modules is correct and "the runtime is ahead of
#      the file". All true — but it was an argument for TOLERATING the failures,
#      and the runner could simply be told which era to judge by instead.
#      `wast.featuresForPath` now runs `proposals/threads/` with that snapshot's
#      feature set (all features minus multi_memory minus multi_table, the
#      latter added as `features.Feature.multi_table` for exactly this purpose),
#      and all 8 pass FOR THE RIGHT REASON rather than being excused.
#
#      🎓 **The lesson is about the baseline, not the runtime: a well-argued
#      entry here is still an entry.** These 8 had the best reasoning in the
#      file and were still closable — the argument justified the score without
#      anyone asking whether the RUNNER was doing its job. Re-read group 1 with
#      that in mind before assuming it is permanent.
#
#      Verified with all three totals, per the rule that a failure diff cannot
#      see a pass that became a skip: 62,890 -> 62,898 passed, 89 -> 81 failed,
#      965 -> 965 skipped. +8 passes, -8 failures, zero skips gained.
#
#   3. DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS — NONE. There is no longer any line here where
#      wazmrt is knowingly wrong by the spec. The last one was
#      `obsolete-keywords.wast`: wazmrt accepted `anyfunc`, the pre-standard
#      spelling of `funcref`, to keep two MVP-era `.wat` files in the wasmtk
#      corpus assembling. It is now refused as `ObsoleteKeyword`, whose message
#      names the modern spelling — the compatibility hint survives, the
#      deviation does not. Those two corpus files need `funcref`.
#
#   4. DIAGNOSED GAPS IN SHIPPED FUNCTIONALITY — ✅ **BOTH CLOSED 2026-08-17,
#      the same day the group was created. This group is EMPTY.**
#
#      It existed for about an hour and is kept because of what it demonstrated.
#      D4 had to invent it: groups 1–3 all said "not a wazmrt defect", and with
#      custom-descriptors implemented there was no untargeted proposal left to
#      attribute two real defects to. The entry said plainly that **a line here is
#      a debt, not an explanation** — and then, asked "what is left to fix", the
#      answer was to fix them rather than to explain them again.
#
#      `exact-func-import.wast` (1) — ⚠️ **the entry UNDER-DESCRIBED its own item.**
#        It said the linker needed `definingFunc`'s walk, and it did — but the
#        larger half was that EXACT function imports had no encoding at all:
#        descriptor kind `0x20` was unknown to the assembler, decoder and linker,
#        and `(exact <typeuse>)` was not parsed, so the assembler manufactured an
#        implicit type and the file's `assert_unlinkable` PASSED because a
#        manufactured type matches nothing. **A false pass produced by dropping
#        the very feature under test.** A diagnosis written from the failing
#        assertion, not from the feature.
#      `exact.wast` (1) — `(ref exact 0)`: the `exact` former without its parens
#        was silently dropped, because `parseValType` indexed the heap type from
#        the END of the list. Third instance of that pattern in one session.
#
#      **Corpus: 0 FAILURES across all 284 files.**
#
# ✅ **THE BASELINE IS EMPTY AS OF 2026-08-18. THERE ARE NO EXPECTED FAILURES LEFT.**
#
# The last line was `error annotations.wast` — the custom-annotations proposal, whose deliberately
# exotic tokens the LEXER could not read, so the whole file was a runner error and its 71 commands
# never ran. Track A implemented annotations (`(@id …)` is lexed and discarded) and it is now
# 64 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped.
#
# 🏁 **Corpus: 284 files, 63,934 assertions passed, ZERO failed, ZERO skipped, and ZERO files with
# failures or errors.** The `-Dbaseline` gate now means what it says with nothing subtracted: any
# non-zero column is a regression.
#
# ⚠️ **AN EMPTY BASELINE IS THE EASIEST FILE IN THE REPO TO QUIETLY RUIN.** Adding a line here to
# make a build green is the failure mode this file has always invited, and there is no longer a
# single legitimate entry to hide behind. A new line needs a GROUP above it explaining the class it
# belongs to — and if the class is "a wazmrt defect", the honest move is the one 2026-08-17 made
# with group 4: fix the two entries the same day rather than explain them a second time.
